evals.name: Linear pipeline scaffolding
evals.prompt: Create a new AuGENT use case called 'document_summarizer'. It needs one agent that calls GPT-4o to summarize documents and one deterministic node that formats the output. The graph should be linear: format -> summarize -> END. Output all the code files inline.
evals.expected_output: Complete use case code with pyproject.toml, graph.py with DocSummarizerState TypedDict extending BaseWorkflowState, models.py with SummarizerOutput using @SchemaRegistry.register_schema, agents/summarizer.py with SummarizerAgent extending AuGENTAgent, nodes/formatter.py with async def formatter function, and main.py with Orchestrator wiring. All imports use correct framework paths. LLM calls include api_key, workflow_id, and pinned model_version.
assertions: State TypedDict extends BaseWorkflowState using multiple TypedDict inheritance
State uses total=False for all-optional fields
SummarizerOutput model has @SchemaRegistry.register_schema() decorator with matching agent name
SummarizerAgent class extends AuGENTAgent with an agent_name class attribute set
LLMService.call() receives api_key, workflow_id, and model_version parameters
Model version is pinned with date (e.g. 2024-08-06), not floating
build_graph() function uses GraphBuilder from ai_agents_core.orchestration
END is imported from ai_agents_core.orchestration.graph_builder, not from langgraph
main.py calls setup_logging() with usecase_name parameter
No hardcoded API keys — credentials come from os.getenv() or environment variables
Directory structure follows usecases/<name>/ai_agents/ pattern with agents/ and nodes/ subdirectories
pyproject.toml declares ai_agents_core as a dependency

evals.name: Add agent to existing use case
evals.prompt: I have an existing use case at usecases/market_analysis. Add a new LLM agent called 'SentimentAgent' that analyzes sentiment using Claude. It takes articles from state, calls LLM, and returns sentiment scores. Wire it into the graph between the existing 'fetch_articles' and 'generate_report' nodes. Use OpenRouter as provider with model anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-20250514. Output the new and modified code inline.
evals.expected_output: New agent file with SentimentAgent(AuGENTAgent), new schema in models.py, updated graph.py with new node and adjusted edges. All imports correct.
assertions: SentimentAgent class extends AuGENTAgent
agent_name attribute is set on the class
agent_name matches the string passed to @SchemaRegistry.register_schema()
LLMService.call() uses provider parameter or provider-aware configuration
Model name includes explicit version date (20250514 in the model identifier)
Graph edges are updated to: fetch_articles -> sentiment_agent -> generate_report
Existing node definitions and edges are preserved, not removed
Schema import in agent file enables side-effect registration (F401-style)
No existing code patterns are broken or contradicted

evals.name: Conditional branching graph with router
evals.prompt: Build a use case called 'fraud_detector' with a branching graph: node 'transaction_validator' routes to either 'fraud_analyst' (LLM agent, if suspicious) or END (if clean). The fraud_analyst agent calls GPT-4o-mini to analyze suspicious transactions and then goes to 'alert_dispatcher' (deterministic node) which ends the graph. Add proper schema validation and observability. Output all code inline.
evals.expected_output: Complete use case with TransactionValidator as deterministic async function, FraudAnalystAgent as LLM agent with gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18, AlertDispatcher as deterministic node. Graph has conditional edge from transaction_validator with pure router function. Router reads state field, no LLM in routing logic. All output schemas registered. Correct policies per node type.
assertions: Router function is pure — reads state field, makes no LLM or API calls
Conditional edge uses routing_map dict or equivalent with 'fraud_analyst' and END targets
FraudAnalystAgent uses model name gpt-4o-mini with a pinned calendar-date version (not floating)
Agent output schema is registered via @SchemaRegistry.register_schema()
Transaction validator is a plain async def function, not an agent class
All graph paths eventually reach END (no dead ends)
setup_logging() is called in main.py with usecase_name parameter
workflow_id is propagated through every LLM call in the agent

evals.name: RAG use case with FastAPI endpoint
evals.prompt: Create use case 'rag_qa' on auGENT with: a vector search node (deterministic, reads query and returns documents from state), a RAG agent (LLM, takes query plus documents and generates answer), and a FastAPI endpoint at /api/v1/ask that accepts a question and returns the answer. Include proper output schema, observability setup, and health check endpoint. Output all code inline.
evals.expected_output: Complete use case with vector_search.py deterministic node, rag_agent.py with RAGAgent(AuGENTAgent), api/main.py with FastAPI, api/models.py with request/response Pydantic models, main.py CLI entry. Graph is vector_search -> rag_agent -> END. API returns AskResponse with answer field. Health endpoint at /api/v1/health.
assertions: API endpoint at /api/v1/ask is a POST endpoint accepting JSON body with question field
API endpoint returns a response model with an answer field
Health check endpoint exists at /api/v1/health returning status
RAG agent is an AuGENTAgent subclass that uses documents from state in its prompt
Vector search node is deterministic — no LLMService.call(), no OpenAI calls
Agent output schema is registered via @SchemaRegistry.register_schema()
FastAPI request/response models (Pydantic) are separated from output schemas
A CLI entry point (main.py) exists in addition to the API server
setup_logging() is called in both main.py and api/main.py
